technical-data.invention-title: DIFFERENTIAL STAINING OF BACTERIA USING FLUORESCENCE
COLORATION DIFFERENTIELLE DE BACTERIES PAR FLUORESCENCE

abstract.p: This differential staining method allows to distinguish in fluorescence Gram-positive bacteria from Gram-negative bacteria. The method uses two fluorochromes, one acting in the wavelength of red, acridine orange, another acting in the wavelength of green, the fluorescein, forming together a red/green system (red + green = yellow).

Cette technique de coloration différentielle permet de distinguer par fluorescence des bactéries Gram-positives de bactéries Gram-négatives. On utilise, dans le cadre de cette technique, deux fluorochromes, l'un agissant dans la longueur d'ondes du rouge, l'orangé d'acridine, l'autre dans la longueur d'onde du vert, la fluorescéine, et formant ensemble un système rouge/vert (rouge + vert = jaune).

description.p: DIFFERENTIAL STAINING OF BACTERIA USING FLUORESCENCE

Bacteria are unicellular procaryotic microorganisms. Their cellular body is enclosed by a cell wall,which gives them important distinctive features. Usually they are divided into gram-positive bacteria and Gram-negative bacteria (Gram,danish microbiologist,XIX-XX century) because of their cell wall are more or less resistant to decoloration. This differentiation has a clinical,prognostic and therapeutical projection.
In 1980 McCarthy and Senne used a fluorochrome staining to detect microorganisms in direct smears prepared from clinical specimens (e.g. blood) and reported a good sensitivity of this technique.
In fluorescence no staining method is yet available which allows to distinguish Gram-positive from

The staining method here presented allows to distinguish Gram-positive from Gram-negative bacteria in fluorescence and could be used in clinical microbiology because its sensitivity is greater than the
Gram staining technique (e.g. detection of bacteria in blood cultures).

Certain fluorochrome dyes exposed to ultraviolet light emit fluorescent radiation. The principle is based on the absoφtion of a photon by the fluorochrome with utilization of the light for a jump of an electron from a low energy level to a higher energy level (exciting state).
The purpose of the technique is to have a differential staining effect between Gram-positive and

Gram-negative bacteria in fluorescence. We acheived it using two fluorochromes ,one acting in the wavelength of red,acridine orange,another acting in the wavelength of green,the fluorescein,forming together a red/green system (e.g. red+green=yellow). Because ethyl alcohol/acetone (50%-50%) decoloration produces only little differences on bacteria stained with the fluorochrome acridine orange (0,01%) to reveal these differences we used a chromatic system,the red/green system. We get it adding a second green fluorochrome,the fluorescein (0,002%). The bacteria which are more resistant to decoloration (Gram-positive bacteria) will keep a sufficient share of acridine orange to form a red/green system and will result yellow for the combination of the two colours when adding this share of red to the share of green of the second fluorochrome,the fluorescein. Instead the bacteria
which are less resistant (Gram-negative bacteria) cannot do it and they appear in the exceeding second green colour.

the slides were prepared by first placing a drop of distilled water and then applying the samples of culture. The smears were subsequently air dried and fixed with heat. The bacterial species were obtained from routine cultures and were grown for 24-48 h . Other pure bacterial species were grown in agar into sterile collection tubes.Bacterial strains,representing 25 different species, 12 Gram- positive and 13 Gram-negative, were tested.

It is recommended to take care of correct procedure : staining times,decoloration time and washes,above all,the final wash must be respected accurately. The staining method should be performed on young (24-48 h.) cultures.

The bacteria which are more resistant to decoloration (Gram-positive bacteria) kept a sufficient share of acridine orange to form a red/green system and they resulted yellow ,for the combination of the two colours when adding this share of red to the share of green of the second fluorochrome,the
fluorescein. Instead,bacteria which were less resistant (Gram-negative bacteria) did not keep enough acridine and they appeared in the second exceeding green colour.

claim.claim-text: 1) This differential staining method in fluorescence is simple to use,has no toxicity;moreover the differences between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria are always clear and easy to detect.

2) This new staining method in fluorescence is more sensitive than the Gram stain and its use may be recommended in microbiological search and diagnosis (for example to examine blood cultures coming from septicaemic patients,in these cases rapid bacterial strain identification is crucial).
